article.headline: ServiceNow Gains As Market Falls; Exec Calls Defense A Major Driver
article.deck: The stock is 6.2% past the 149.70 buy point of a seven-week cup and beyond the 157.19 top of the buy range, so it is extended.
body: ServiceNow sells cloud software that runs the routine work inside large organizations: IT service and asset management, security operations, risk management, customer service and field service, human resources, and legal and contract work. The pitch is a single platform for the processes that tie a company's departments together.

Revenue is the growth story. Sales rose 24.0% to $3.987 billion in the June quarter, and revenue has risen in each quarter in the table: $3.407 billion in September 2025, $3.568 billion in December and $3.770 billion in March. Earnings have not kept pace. June-quarter EPS fell 21.6% to 29 cents, after 48 cents, 38 cents and 45 cents in the three prior quarters.

The market is paying for the sales line. ServiceNow carries a market value of $164.3 billion and trades at 99.4 times trailing earnings and 31.8 times forward earnings. A Saturday headline asked whether agentic AI growth can justify a premium 80x earnings multiple when the company reports on Oct. 28.

Friday the stock rose 1.96, or 1.2%, to 158.96 on volume 0.8x its 50-day average, while all three major indexes fell; a Friday headline noted it advanced as the market declined. It cleared the 149.70 buy point of a seven-week cup on Oct. 21, on volume 0.95x average. The cup is 15.3% deep, with a high on Aug. 31 and a low on Sept. 28. Two sessions later the close sits 6.2% above the buy point, past the 157.19 top of the buy range. The stock is extended, and the entry is gone until a new base or a pullback to a moving average.

The cup formed after a long slide from 210.20 in July 2025 to 81.24 in April, and the stock remains below that earlier high and 17.6% under its 52-week high of 192.97. It is 15.6% above the 50-day line at 137.49 and 1.55 ATRs above the 21-day line at 144.23, a firm trend that is not yet stretched. RS rank is 90 of 99 on the desk's list, though the RS line is 25.4% below its high. The stock is up 50.6% in three months and 3.8% year to date, and down 15.1% over a year.
The news gives one business thread beyond the earnings date. A Friday headline said a ServiceNow executive at AUSA called the defense business a 'major driver' over the next year.
The Oct. 28 report is the next test of the chart. Revenue growth has carried the stock off its April low, and the last quarter's EPS went the other way.
article.watch: The Oct. 28 earnings report, with the 21-day line at 144.23 as the first support below.

article.headline: HubSpot Extends Rally On Earnings Upgrades Ahead Of Nov. 4 Report
article.deck: HubSpot is 2.2% above the 265.10 buy point of a seven-week cup, inside a buy range that runs to 278.36.
body: HubSpot rose 3.69, or 1.4%, to 270.88 Friday on light volume, 0.59x its 50-day average. It cleared the 265.10 buy point of a seven-week cup Thursday, on volume 0.91x average. The cup is 28.3% deep, with a high on Aug. 31 and a low on Sept. 28. The close sits 2.2% above the buy point, with the buy range running to 278.36.

The cup sits inside a far larger decline, from 568.16 in July 2025 to 169.63 in June, and the stock is 45.6% below its 52-week high of 497.96. It is 16.4% above the 50-day line at 232.80 and 2.0 ATRs above the 21-day line at 236.79. The 50-day line still sits just under the 200-day at 234.56. RS rank is 59 of 99 on the desk's list; the RS line is 50.8% below its high. Shares are down 32.5% year to date and up 22.3% in a month.

June-quarter revenue rose 19.8% to $911.74 million, with EPS of 86 cents. Revenue has risen each quarter in the table, from $809.518 million in the September 2025 quarter. The company said it will report third-quarter results on Nov. 4. HubSpot trades at 16.1 times forward earnings, with a market value of $13.9 billion.
Headlines tied the rise to strong growth and earnings upgrades, and a Thursday headline asked why the stock rallied that day.
A close back under 265.10 would undo the breakout before the report.
article.watch: The Nov. 4 earnings report, with 265.10 as the level to hold.

article.headline: CrowdStrike Leaps 8.2% In Cybersecurity Rally; CEO Warns Of Attack Wave
article.deck: CrowdStrike has no base on the desk's chart and no buy point; it bounced off the 50-day line and sits 10.3% below its 52-week high.
body: CrowdStrike jumped 19.63, or 8.2%, to 257.57 Friday on volume 1.31x its 50-day average, the largest gain among the day's stories. The session's low tested the 50-day line at 234.80 and the stock closed 9.7% above it. The desk finds no base on the chart, so there is no buy point to quote.

The close is 10.3% below the 52-week high of 286.99. The session's range reached the 21-day line at 247.34, a reading of 0.0 ATRs from the 21-day line. RS rank is 97 of 99 on the desk's list, and the RS line is 5.3% below its high. Shares are up 119.8% year to date and 106.0% over a year, though down 0.8% over the past month.

July-quarter revenue rose 25.8% to $1.471 billion, with EPS of 1 cent. Revenue has climbed each quarter in the table, from $1.234 billion in the October 2025 quarter. The next report is due Dec. 1. CrowdStrike carries a market value of $263.7 billion and trades at 159.9 times forward earnings.

Friday headlines said Palo Alto and CrowdStrike jumped 6% as an Evercore survey flagged stronger cyber demand. A Saturday headline said CrowdStrike's CEO says a wave of cyberattacks is coming, and another asked about a reported $500 million security deal.
A new base, or a pullback that holds the 50-day line, would give the chart a defined entry.
article.watch: Whether the stock holds the 50-day line at 234.80 while it builds a base.

market_note: The S&P 500 fell 0.5% to 7,623.68 Friday, the Nasdaq slipped 0.2% to 25,955.34 and the Dow dropped 1.2% to 52,215.16. All three closed below their 50-day lines: the S&P 500 by 1.0%, the Nasdaq by 2.4% and the Dow by 0.2%. The S&P 500 carries 5 distribution days over the last 25 sessions, the Nasdaq 3 and the Dow 4, and the desk's state is Market in correction. Leadership is narrow but present: eight names broke out this week, led by software (ServiceNow, monday.com, HubSpot) and big names such as Apple, Spotify and Berkshire Hathaway, software leads the groups with 80% of its names above the 50-day line and energy has 71% above, while only 12% of AI chip names and 6% of AI infrastructure names hold above that line.

chief.verdict: The leadership is narrow and the breakouts are mostly low quality: HUBS cleared its pivot on 0.91 times average volume, MNDY and HUBS come out of 28.3% deep cups sitting 49.4% and 45.6% below their highs, and NOW and FTNT are already past their buy points with earnings on 2026-10-28. The real strength is in energy (71% of the group above the 50-day) and the cyber names bouncing off their 50-day lines, while ai chips (12%) and ai infra (6%) are breaking down. The tight, well-built bases are AAPL and DVN. With the indexes below their 50-day lines, the risk is to the downside.
chief.market: With the Big Picture at Market in correction, 5 distribution days on the S&P 500 and 3 on the Nasdaq, and the Nasdaq 2.4% below its 50-day line, keep exposure light: one or two small starter positions at most, and cut fast.

picks.why: This is the tightest base on the board: a 4-week flat base only 5.7% deep, cleared on 2026-10-22 on 1.17 times average volume, at a new high with the RS line just 1.3% off its own high. The stock is only 0.7% past the 345.44 buy point, so you are not chasing. The risk is earnings on 2026-11-02, which leaves little time to build a cushion, and Friday's volume was light at 0.98 times average.
picks.entry: Buy at or above the 345.44 buy point and no higher than 362.71, as long as it holds above 345.44 on rising volume; it fails if it closes back inside the base and toward the 50-day at 329.47.

picks.why: Friday's low touched the 50-day line, then the stock closed up 4.5% on 1.22 times average volume. That is a live 50-day bounce inside a 29-week cup, with RS rank 84 and an energy group that is working. Earnings are 2026-11-05, outside the next five sessions. The risk is the RS line, still 17.6% below its high, and the 24.1% depth, so this is a starter position, not a full one.
picks.entry: Start a small position above today's high of 51.79 with the 50-day at 48.53 as the stop; add only on a move through the 52.81 buy point on volume, buy range to 55.45.

picks.why: RS rank 93, and a 7.2% rally off the 50-day line at 370.35 shows big money defending it. But the original breakout on 2026-10-02 came on only 0.79 times average volume and failed back into the base, and the stock is 4.6% below the 398.98 buy point.
picks.entry: Wait for a reclaim of 398.98 on volume well above average (buy range to 418.93); a close below the 50-day at 370.35 takes it off the list.

picks.why: This is a proper 27-week cup with RS rank 86 and a new high, but the 2026-10-14 breakout came on just 1.0 times average volume. At 183.21 it sits 3.8% past the 176.51 buy point, close to the 185.34 top of the range, with earnings on 2026-10-30.
picks.entry: No new buys this close to the top of the range ahead of earnings; a pullback toward the 21-day line at 172.46 that holds after the report is the place.

avoid.why: It broke out on 0.91 times average volume from a 28.3% deep cup, 45.6% below its 52-week high, with the RS line 50.8% off its high: no institutional push behind it.
The cup is 28.3% deep, the stock is 49.4% below its high and 18.7% above its 50-day, and Friday's volume dried up to 0.67 times average at 106.53, almost at the 107.2 buy limit.
It is 5.6% past the 170.45 buy point, above the 178.97 limit, with earnings on 2026-10-28, four sessions out: a gamble on the report, not a base entry.
The earnings gap cleared 576.1 on 3.1 times volume, but RS rank is 69, the RS line is 24.0% off its high, the stock is down 13.5% over a year, and it is already 11.1% above its 50-day.
